/.name: bin
/.description: Essential user commands needed by shell/scripts.

/.name: boot
/.description: Kernel and bootloader files used at startup.

/.name: dev
/.description: Device files for disks, terminals, and pseudo-devices.

/.description: Temporary manual mount points for admins.

/.name: run
/.description: Volatile runtime state (PID, sockets, service data).

/.name: srv

/.name: sys
/.description: Kernel object and device model interface.

/.name: usr
/.description: Userland programs, libraries, docs, and shared assets.

/.description: Variable data: logs, cache, spool, state.

/usr.name: bin
/usr.description: Most user commands installed by packages.

/usr.description: Libraries used by programs in /usr/bin and /usr/sbin.

/usr.name: local
/usr.description: Admin-installed software outside package manager control.

/usr.name: src
/usr.description: Optional source code or kernel source trees.

/boot.description: Initial RAM disk used at boot.

/dev.name: null

/var.description: System and application logs for troubleshooting.

/var.description: Rebuildable cached data to improve performance.

/var.description: User mailboxes (on systems using local mail storage).

/etc.description: Secured password hashes and account aging rules.

/etc.description: Filesystem mount definitions used during boot.

/etc.name: systemd
/etc.description: Systemd unit files, drop-ins, and service overrides.

/etc.name: network
/etc.description: Network interface and routing configuration (distro dependent).
